title: One-horn extension of a categorical enlargement with fixed three-horn restriction
statement: Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, horns and degreewise pullbacks from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations and cocartesian edges from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and categorical equivalences from [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Put $H=\Lambda^3_2$ with inclusion $\iota:H\hookrightarrow\Delta^3$. Let $r:E\to H$ be an inner fibration such that every vertex over 1 is the source of an $r$-cocartesian edge over $1\to2$, where cocartesian means the outer-horn lifting condition for this arbitrary simplicial base. Let $s:S\to\Delta^3$ be a map of small simplicial sets and $u:E\hookrightarrow S$ a monomorphism with $su=\iota r$, such that $u$ is a categorical equivalence and the canonical map $E\to S\times_{\Delta^3}H$ is an isomorphism. Fix $n\geq2$, $0<i<n$, and a simplicial map $\alpha:\Lambda_i^n\to S$. Then there are a small simplicial set $S_\alpha$ over $\Delta^3$ and a monomorphism $v:S\hookrightarrow S_\alpha$ over $\Delta^3$ such that $v$ is a categorical equivalence, the canonical map $E\to S_\alpha\times_{\Delta^3}H$ induced by $vu$ is an isomorphism, and $v\alpha$ extends to a simplicial map $\Delta^n\to S_\alpha$. No quasicategory or simultaneous filling of other horns is asserted for $S_\alpha$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.4, printed pp.331-332: the individual-extension subclaim (i-prime), (ii-prime), in the induction where E -> C(m) is already a categorical equivalence with unchanged horn pullback. The final K2-gluing verification has a compatibility gap recorded in the second-reading report; this technical subclaim remains unsplit. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Factor $s:S\to\Delta^3$ as a trivial cofibration $j:S\hookrightarrow T$ followed by a Joyal fibration $t:T\to\Delta^3$, using [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. The standard simplex $\Delta^3$ is a quasicategory: its simplices are monotone vertex strings, and an inner horn specifies exactly the compatible ordered vertices, whose string supplies its filler. Composing the lifting properties of $t$ and $\Delta^3\to *$ shows that $T$ is fibrant, hence a quasicategory. The composite $w=ju:E\hookrightarrow T$ is a categorical equivalence by two-out-of-three. Choose a filler $b:\Delta^n\to T$ of $j\alpha$ using the quasicategory definition. Its base map $tb$ restricts to $s\alpha$ on the horn. Set $R=T\times_{\Delta^3}H$ and view $E$ as a simplicial subset of $R$ through $w$. All factorizations and these objects remain in the given small universe.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.4, individual-extension subclaim on printed pp.331-332; agent replacement by facewise retraction and a degreewise pushout. The printed K2 gluing is not used.

proof.text: For each nonempty face $\sigma=\Delta^J\subseteq H$, put $E_\sigma=E\times_H\sigma$ and $R_\sigma=R\times_H\sigma=T\times_{\Delta^3}\sigma$. The map $w$ satisfies every hypothesis of [lem-coef-cocartesian-three-horn-face-conservation]: $r$ is the original inner fibration, its cocartesian lifts over $1\to2$ are unchanged, $T$ is a small quasicategory, and $w$ is a monomorphism and categorical equivalence over $\Delta^3$. Consequently $E_\sigma\hookrightarrow R_\sigma$ is a categorical equivalence for every such face. This uses face conservation as a comparison theorem, not any asserted strict horn pullback for $T$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.4, individual-extension subclaim on printed pp.331-332; agent replacement by facewise retraction and a degreewise pushout. The printed K2 gluing is not used.

proof.text: For every simplicial subcomplex $L\subseteq H$ generated by a collection of its nondegenerate faces, the inclusion $E_L\hookrightarrow R_L$ is a categorical equivalence, where subscripts mean inverse images. Prove this by induction on the number of faces of $L$. It holds for $L=\varnothing$ by identity, and for a simplex by step 2. Otherwise remove a maximal face $\sigma$, writing $L=L_0\cup\sigma$ and $L_0\cap\sigma=\partial\sigma$. Inverse images give the two pushout spans $(E_{L_0}\leftarrow E_{\partial\sigma}\to E_\sigma)$ and $(R_{L_0}\leftarrow R_{\partial\sigma}\to R_\sigma)$. Their intersection and $L_0$ comparisons are equivalences by induction; the $\sigma$ comparison is step 2. Apply [lem-coef-model-cofibrant-colimit-comparison](b) in the Joyal model structure: all six objects are cofibrant because every initial map of simplicial sets is monic, both attaching maps are monic, and all three comparison maps are weak equivalences. Their pushout comparison is exactly $E_L\to R_L$ degreewise. In particular $E\hookrightarrow R$ and every $E_{\partial\sigma}\hookrightarrow R_{\partial\sigma}$ are categorical equivalences.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.4, individual-extension subclaim on printed pp.331-332; agent replacement by facewise retraction and a degreewise pushout. The printed K2 gluing is not used.

proof.text: For each face $\sigma\subseteq H$, the projection $r_\sigma:E_\sigma\to\sigma$ is an inner fibration: any inner lifting square is a square for $r$ with its prescribed base simplex in $\sigma$, so its lift also lies in the pullback. Both $\sigma$ and $E_\sigma$ are quasicategories: $\sigma$ has the ordered-vertex fillers described in step 1, and a horn in $E_\sigma$ first fills in $\sigma$ and then lifts through $r$. Every equivalence edge of $\sigma$ is an identity, since its inverse would give two opposite inequalities between its endpoints; the corresponding degenerate edge in $E_\sigma$ is an equivalence lift with prescribed source. Thus [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations](1), applied only between these quasicategories, says that $r_\sigma$ is a Joyal fibration. This conclusion is not asserted for $r:E\to H$, whose base need not be a quasicategory.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.4, individual-extension subclaim on printed pp.331-332; agent replacement by facewise retraction and a degreewise pushout. The printed K2 gluing is not used.

proof.text: Construct a retraction $\rho:R\to E$ over $H$, equal to the identity on $E$, by processing the nondegenerate faces of $H$ in increasing dimension. The initial map on $R_\varnothing=\varnothing$ is unique. Suppose compatible maps have been chosen over all proper faces of a face $\sigma$. They glue on $R_{\partial\sigma}$ and agree with the identity on $E_{\partial\sigma}$. Thus they and $\operatorname{id}_{E_\sigma}$ define a map $M_\sigma=E_\sigma\amalg_{E_{\partial\sigma}}R_{\partial\sigma}\to E_\sigma$ over $\sigma$. All these unions are degreewise. The inclusion $E_\sigma\to M_\sigma$ is a pushout of the monomorphic categorical equivalence $E_{\partial\sigma}\to R_{\partial\sigma}$ from step 3, hence a trivial cofibration: diagonal lifts extend across the pushout by the weak factorization system in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. The inclusion $M_\sigma\hookrightarrow R_\sigma$ is monic, since the intersection is exactly $E_{\partial\sigma}$, and is a categorical equivalence by two-out-of-three with step 2. Lift it against the Joyal fibration $r_\sigma$ from step 4 to extend to $R_\sigma\to E_\sigma$. Faces of the same dimension overlap only in previously processed faces, so the extensions agree there. After the finitely many vertices, edges and triangles, these maps glue to $\rho$ over all of $H$. Since $\rho w=\operatorname{id}_E$ and $E\to R$ is an equivalence by step 3, $\rho$ is a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.4, individual-extension subclaim on printed pp.331-332; agent replacement by facewise retraction and a degreewise pushout. The printed K2 gluing is not used.

proof.text: Form the degreewise pushout $P=T\amalg_R E$ using the inclusion $R\hookrightarrow T$ and the retraction $\rho:R\to E$. Both maps are over $\Delta^3$, so $P$ has a map to $\Delta^3$. The map $a:T\to P$ is a categorical equivalence by [lem-coef-all-cofibrant-left-proper], applied to the Joyal model structure: every simplicial set is cofibrant, $R\hookrightarrow T$ is a cofibration, and $\rho$ is a weak equivalence. Consequently $v=aj:S\to P$ is a categorical equivalence. Small degreewise pushouts stay in the fixed universe. Finally $ab:\Delta^n\to P$ is the required filler, since $(ab)|_{\Lambda_i^n}=aj\alpha=v\alpha$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.4, individual-extension subclaim on printed pp.331-332; agent replacement by facewise retraction and a degreewise pushout. The printed K2 gluing is not used.

proof.text: Check the strict assertions degreewise, rather than inferring them from an equivalence. Since $R\hookrightarrow T$ is an inclusion, the pushout set in degree $k$ is the disjoint union $P_k=(T_k\setminus R_k)\amalg E_k$, with $a$ equal to the identity on the first summand and to $\rho$ on $R_k$. A simplex of $T_k\setminus R_k$ has base outside $H_k$; a simplex of $E_k$ has base in $H_k$. Hence the inverse image $P\times_{\Delta^3}H$ is canonically $E$, in every degree and with all operators. Also $j(S_k)\cap R_k=j(u(E_k))$ because $E\to S\times_{\Delta^3}H$ is an isomorphism. On this intersection $aj$ is the identity identification with $E_k$, and outside it $aj$ lands injectively in the other summand. Thus $v$ is monic. On $E$ the composite $vu=aju$ is exactly the inclusion of the second summand, so the isomorphism just found is the canonical one in the statement. Taking $S_\alpha=P$ completes all clauses.
